newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan June long-term prime rate seen steady - banker.
newsitem.headline: Japan June long-term prime rate seen steady - banker.

text.p: Japan's long-term prime lending rate is expected to be left unchanged at 3.1 percent in June from the previous month, a senior long-term credit bank official said on Friday.
The prime rate, which is applied to loans of one year and longer to Japanese long-term credit banks' most creditworthy clients, is reviewed every month, reflecting market trends.
The Industrial Bank of Japan Ltd said it would announce its June prime rate on Monday, as well as the coupon rate of the bank's new five-year debenture to be issued this month.

The IBJ customarily sets its prime rate 0.9 percentage point above the coupon rate of its five-year debenture, which is issued monthly and is the benchmark in Japan's debenture market. Bank debentures are the long-term credit banks' major fund-raising tool.
IBJ's May 2.20 percent five-year debenture was traded at a yield of 2.10 percent on Friday, after trading at 2.11 percent on Thursday.

The other two long-term credit banks -- the Long-Term Credit Bank of Japan Ltd and Nippon Credit Bank Ltd -- are expected to announce their prime rates and the terms of their June debentures on Tuesday, traders said.
